hero.headline: Authentic Korean-Japanese
hero.sub: August Moon cooks authentic Korean-Japanese cuisine on East Main Street in Norristown. The room holds a sushi bar. BBQ party trays are how larger tables eat. Phone orders are how a lot of the food leaves. Lunch and dinner run on the hours from their order page. Sunday the restaurant is closed.

items.title: Korean-Japanese in one room
items.text: The restaurant calls the food authentic Korean-Japanese. You can eat across both kitchens in one visit: Korean plates and Japanese sushi from the same East Main Street address.

items.title: Sushi bar
items.text: A sushi bar is part of the room. Rolls and nigiri are ordered there, not as a side note on a purely Korean menu.

items.title: BBQ party trays and phone orders
items.text: BBQ party trays are built for a table, not a single bowl. Phone orders are a published path: you call, you set the ticket, you pick up or sit down when the kitchen has it.

story.heading: East Main Street, two cuisines
paragraphs: August Moon is a Norristown restaurant that refuses to pick only Korea or only Japan. Authentic Korean-Japanese is their own phrase. The sushi bar and the BBQ party trays are how that phrase looks on a table. Phone orders keep the kitchen usable when you are not walking in cold.

Lunch is a shorter window on weekdays. Dinner stretches later on Friday and Saturday. Sunday they close. Those hours come from their order page, so the page you are reading will not invent a brunch or a late-night service they did not publish.

experience.heading: How a meal actually gets to the table

items.title: Call the ticket in
items.text: Phone orders are how many tables start. You call August Moon, you name the Korean plates, the sushi, or the BBQ party tray, and the kitchen works that ticket.

items.title: Sit the sushi bar or the table
items.text: The sushi bar is a real station in the room. A party tray is for the larger table that wants Korean BBQ in a shared format.

items.title: Lunch window, then dinner
items.text: Weekday lunch is 11:30am to 2pm. Dinner returns in the late afternoon. Saturday dinner starts at 4pm. Sunday there is no service.

feature.heading: Sushi bar and BBQ party trays
feature.text: Those two formats are the restaurant in physical form. One is a bar of Japanese work. The other is a Korean BBQ tray built for a group. Authentic Korean-Japanese means both are in the same Norristown room.

spotlight.heading: Phone orders are part of the kitchen
spotlight.text: August Moon publishes phone orders as a way in. You do not have to discover the menu only by walking East Main Street. Call, name the tray or the sushi, and let the kitchen cook.
